task_message:
Case V49: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 131x131x97 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case V49 is finished.

**What I did:**
1. **Located the lesion** with axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets: a T2-hyperintense, lobulated soft-tissue mass in the limb (largest cross-section ≈30×25 mm, with a bright rim/capsule and darker central core, plus a continuous elongated bright extension running along the limb axis toward the bone/vascular bundle).
2. **Seeded the model** with a single positive point on the mass at axial 44 → initial mask v1 (10.7 mL, 1 component).
3. **Verified in all three planes** (axial 25/30/35/42/44/52/55/61/70/75/79/84, coronal 62/66/75, sagittal 55/63/73/79 with outline/fill overlays): confirmed the mask follows the bright mass and its continuous extension, without including the separate superficial bright band proposed as candidate C1.
4. **Refined and cleaned** the mask (seg_refine, then keep_component to remove the small distant specks), giving a single connected 10.7 mL mask spanning axial 28–84, coronal 46–85, sagittal 48–79.
5. **Final review**: no lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange) on any of the three planes; rejected candidate C1 (separate superficial structure, not contiguous with the lesion) and saved with confidence **medium** — the main mass boundary is convincing, but the far distal tapering tail is the least certain portion.
